clue.text: Cause of cloudiness that affects visibility in fall

definitions.text: Cause of cloudiness that affects visibility
definitions.meaning: an eye condition in which the lens clouds over and sight is dimmed
a great waterfall, especially one with a steep drop

explanation.surface: Something that clouds the view in autumn, perhaps fog drifting down as the leaves fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' looks like the season, which fits the calendar theme, but here it is a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The eye disease clouds the lens; the waterfall sense is a large, steep cascade of water.

clue.text: Help for speaker that comes before November

definitions.meaning: a microphone, which amplifies someone giving a speech
in the radio phonetic alphabet the code word for M sits just before the one for N, November

explanation.surface: A calendar hint: something useful to a public speaker that arrives before the month of November.
explanation.walkthrough: November is not the month here but the radio code word for N; the letter before it is M, whose code word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is informal shorthand for a microphone, a speaker's aid, and the NATO alphabet code word for M.

clue.text: Heart specialist's trick taking in Republican on the Fourth of July

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means this piece sits on top of the following one
taking in means the word for trick swallows the Republican abbreviation

parts.note: to have someone is to trick or fool them

indicators.note: Fourth of picks the fourth letter of the word July

explanation.surface: A cardiologist pulls a stunt involving a Republican politician on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth of July' reads as the US holiday but just asks for the fourth letter of July. William Harvey, the 17th-century English physician, discovered how blood circulates.
explanation.definitionFit: William Harvey described the circulation of the blood driven by the heart, making him a famous cardiac pioneer.

clue.text: Information on courses, some tribally set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden run is read from the bottom upwards
some means only part of the words tribally set is used, a run hidden across them

explanation.surface: Details of course content, partly arranged on tribal lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' looks like a phrasal verb but 'set' is part of the hiding place and 'up' turns the hidden letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabuses are outlines of what a course of study covers, so they inform students about courses.

clue.text: You can't miss it on board at sea before year's end

indicators.note: before puts the jumble ahead of the final letter
at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled
end picks the final letter of the word year

explanation.surface: Something unmissable aboard a ship at sea just before New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumble of ONBOARD makes BARNDOO, and R from 'year's end' completes it. 'Can't hit a barn door' is said of a hopeless shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn door is the proverbially huge target that even the worst marksman could not fail to hit.

clue.text: Names dynasty one's located among offspring being raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, being raised means the whole assembly is read upwards
located among means the dynasty and one's sit inside the word for offspring

parts.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants
the Tang were a Chinese imperial dynasty
one's is read as one is, I plus S

explanation.surface: A royal dynasty is named, one member found among the children being brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being raised' reads as children being brought up, but in this down clue it turns the whole assembly upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate someone is to name or appoint them, so it works as a verb meaning names.

clue.text: Oktoberfest setting for local by replacing TV, bit by bit, in pub

indicators.note: bit by bit says the swap is one letter at a time, B for T and Y for V
replacing means the letters of by take the place of T and V in the word for pub

parts.note: a tavern is an inn or pub
the first of the two letters T and V, as printed; the second is swapped next
the first of the two letters B and Y, as printed; Y replaces V next

explanation.surface: A local's name for where the Munich beer festival is held, made by switching the TV in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: B replaces T and Y replaces V in TAVERN. 'for local' means the name locals use: Bayern is the German for Bavaria.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich's Oktoberfest takes place in Bavaria, which German speakers call Bayern.

clue.text: For middle of month, put in one unknown soldier, historically

indicators.note: For here means instead of: the new letters stand in for the middle of month
put in means the replacement letters are inserted where the middle was

parts.note: January is a month, whose middle letter is U
I is the Roman numeral one
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: In mid-month, one unidentified soldier is enlisted, a historical footnote.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of JANUARY, U, is swapped for I and Z. Janizaries (or janissaries) were the Ottoman sultan's elite infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Janissaries were the Ottoman Empire's elite foot soldiers, disbanded in 1826, so the word is historical.

clue.text: Back a time and a place for events

indicators.note: Back means the word for a time is read in reverse

parts.note: an era is a period or time
N is a shortened and, as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: Going back to a certain time and place where things happened.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a venue or enclosed space where sports, shows or contests are staged.

clue.text: Dramatically it follows the winter's end, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for end is spoken, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a tail is the end or back part of something

explanation.surface: Something trails the end of winter, as we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatically' points to Shakespeare's play The Winter's Tale, where this word follows 'The Winter's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late romance is titled The Winter's Tale, so in drama this word comes after those two.

clue.text: Some February mail — around middle of month lets naive get excited?

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters surround the middle of month
letters that get excited are stirred up and rearranged
middle of picks the central letter of the word month

explanation.surface: Mid-February's post gets an innocent soul worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get excited' rearranges LETSNAIVE into VALETINES, placed around N, the middle of 'month'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards sent on 14 February to sweethearts are a seasonal part of the post that month.

clue.text: Springtime festival's call for help

definitions.meaning: the first of May, a traditional spring holiday; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A spring celebration turns out to be a cry for help.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of May is a spring holiday, and the distress call comes from French m'aider, help me.

clue.text: Russian revolutionary's exceptionally discreet about doctor

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the doctor abbreviation
exceptionally suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A Russian rebel is unusually tight-lipped about a medic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exceptionally' rearranges DISCREET into DECERIST, which goes 'about' MB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Decembrists were Russian army officers who led a failed revolt against the tsar in December 1825.

clue.text: British admitting poet wanting to return in April

definitions.text: poet wanting to return in April

parts.note: owning is admitting, as in owning up

explanation.surface: A Brit confesses to a poet's longing to come home in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning's poem Home-Thoughts, from Abroad begins 'Oh, to be in England / Now that April's there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Browning wrote longingly from Italy of being back in England in April, a famous expression of homesickness.

clue.text: Be scrupulous with slight touch after start of summer

indicators.note: after puts the light touch behind the first letter
start of picks the opening letter of the word summer

parts.note: a tickle is a light touch

explanation.surface: Be careful, with only the lightest of touches once summer begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To stickle is to insist fussily on small points, being overly particular about details.

clue.text: Test ground with it, as rule

parts.note: Lord's in London is a cricket ground that stages Test matches
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A cricket venue that's up to date, as it were, laid down as a rule.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the famous London cricket ground where international Test matches are played.
explanation.definitionFit: A lordship is dominion or authority over people or land, so it can mean rule.

clue.text: March, perhaps, for international event

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: A month of the year, perhaps chosen for some global event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month, fitting the calendar theme, but it is a demonstration. 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A protest march is one example of a public demonstration of objection.

clue.text: Violently attacked about pound being rescued

indicators.note: about means the word for violently attacked goes round the pound abbreviation

parts.note: savaged means mauled or violently attacked
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone savagely beaten over a pound is then saved.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage is to save goods or wreckage from loss, so salvaged things have been recovered.

clue.text: Upset last month over mail being misdirected, it's asserted

indicators.note: over means the reversed month spreads round the jumbled post
in a down clue, Upset means the abbreviation for last month is turned upside down

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the year's last month

indicators.note: post that is misdirected is sent astray, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that December's post went astray, they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like an emotion but turns the month upside down in this down clue; 'over' then has it wrap the scrambled post.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim something is to state it as true, so a claimed fact is one that has been asserted.

clue.text: Said with relief where royalty goes in summer sometimes

definitions.text: where royalty goes in summer sometimes

indicators.note: with joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: a balm is something that soothes, a relief
oral means spoken, said aloud

explanation.surface: Spoken with a sigh of relief about where the royals spend their summer holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: BALMORAL Castle is the British royal family's Scottish estate, used in late summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal family traditionally spends its late-summer break at Balmoral Castle in Aberdeenshire.

clue.text: A flurry about Burmese title that's imposing

indicators.note: about means A and the flurry word together go round the Burmese title

parts.note: a gust is a sudden flurry of wind
U is a Burmese honorific for a man, as in U Thant

explanation.surface: A sudden fuss over a Burmese dignitary that is rather grand.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means majestic or venerable, inspiring awe and respect.

clue.text: Saint seen in one page of annual publication? In a way that's fair

indicators.note: seen in means the saint abbreviation appears inside the calendar page

parts.note: a calendar is published annually with a page per month; July is one such page

explanation.surface: A saint pictured on one page of a yearly calendar, and that's only right.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting fairly means acting with justice, so the adverb describes treatment that is deserved.

clue.text: Place in Alaska where gold's found after start of summer

indicators.note: found after puts the gold symbol after the month

parts.note: June begins the summer in the northern hemisphere
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A spot in Alaska where gold turned up as summer began, a nod to the gold rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of summer' looks like a first-letter pick but is the whole month that summer begins with.
explanation.definitionFit: Juneau is the state capital of Alaska, founded after gold was discovered there in 1880.

clue.text: Frantically organises to contain end of spring hostility

indicators.note: to contain means the jumble holds the last letter of spring
done frantically, in a wild hurry, so the letters are thrown into disorder
end of picks the final letter of the word spring

explanation.surface: Someone madly arranges things to keep a lid on the tension that builds as spring closes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantically' rearranges ORGANISES into AGRESSION, which takes in G from the 'end of spring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggression is hostile or violent behaviour towards others, a synonym for hostility.

clue.text: Stretch between spring and end of autumn

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word autumn

explanation.surface: The stretch of time between spring and the end of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is the full extent or length of something, a stretch of distance or time.

clue.text: Short part of year for some Irish clan

definitions.meaning: a branch of a family or clan, especially in Ireland

explanation.surface: A brief stretch of the year for certain Irish families.
explanation.definitionFit: Sept is the abbreviation for September and also an Irish word for a clan or family group.

clue.text: Our group on board? Reduced fare from Japan

indicators.note: on means our group is placed aboard, inside the shortened vessel
Reduced means the word for vessel loses its last letter

parts.note: to be on board is to be on a ship, so board stands for the vessel
us is the group that includes the speaker

explanation.surface: A cruise passenger asks if the group is aboard, then sees cut-price Japanese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' looks like a price cut on the fare, but it docks the vessel's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, so it is food from Japan.

clue.text: Specimens one removed from tall buildings after test

indicators.note: after puts the shortened buildings behind the test

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: removed from means the numeral for one is taken out of the word for tall buildings

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Samples taken from a tower block once an inspection is done.
explanation.walkthrough: A pile is a grand or massive building, a sense solvers may not expect for tall buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples and specimens are both individual items that represent their kind.
